description: routes/search.ts builds the product search query with raw string interpolation: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%${criteria}%' OR description LIKE '%${criteria}%') AND deletedAt IS NULL) ORDER BY name, with no parameterization at all on the q query-string parameter. The Products table has 9 columns, determined live by incrementing a UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,... payload until the column-count error disappeared. A single unauthenticated GET request with a UNION SELECT payload appended to q dumps either every user's email and password hash from the Users table, or the full CREATE TABLE definition of every table in the database from sqlite_master, both in the same ordinary-looking JSON search response.
expected_exploit_indicator: An unauthenticated GET to the public product search endpoint, with a UNION SELECT payload in its q parameter, returns every row of the Users table's email/password columns (or every table definition from sqlite_master) inside the normal search-results JSON
expected_blocked_signal: The same payload is rejected before it ever reaches the database, with the search still functioning normally for ordinary search terms
legitimate_check: A normal product search (e.g. for "juice") still returns matching products correctly.
